title: Apple Shares Slip After Hours on Memory Costs Despite Strong iPhone Sales; AMD Reports Tonight
dek: Apple shares fell about 2.8% after its results on Monday, as rising memory costs threatened margins. AMD reports after the close today.
author: Meridian Newsroom

keyPoints: Apple reported after the close on Monday, Nov. 2 (MarketChameleon).
Apple slipped 2.8% after hours as rising memory costs threatened margins, despite strong iPhone sales (Saxo Bank).
Investors reacted to Apple's earnings report as US stock futures were mixed on Tuesday (TheStreet).
AMD is confirmed to report after the close on Tuesday, Nov. 3 (Earnings Whispers, Yahoo Finance).
body:
## Apple: strong iPhone sales, margin worry

Apple reported its results after the close on Monday, Nov. 2 (MarketChameleon). Saxo Bank said the stock slipped 2.8% in after-hours trading as rising memory costs threatened margins, even though iPhone sales were strong (Saxo Bank). TheStreet said futures were mixed as investors reacted to the report (TheStreet).

This edition does not include Apple's reported revenue, earnings per share or guidance. Those figures were not verified from a primary release or a second wire in time for this edition, so they are left out rather than estimated. The next update should add them once the company's release or a wire report confirms them.

## AMD reports tonight

Advanced Micro Devices is set to report after the close on Tuesday. Yahoo Finance said investors will look for signs of AI demand at a time of pressure on the AI trade (Yahoo Finance). Earnings Whispers listed the same date (Earnings Whispers). Saxo Bank listed AMD among today's US earnings, alongside Shopify and Pfizer (Saxo Bank).

## What the after-hours move signals

The reaction came from margins, not from the top line. Saxo Bank described strong iPhone sales alongside the memory-cost problem, which suggests the company is selling well but paying more for the chips and memory that go into its devices (Saxo Bank). When component costs rise faster than prices, analysts usually focus on gross margin guidance and on how much of the cost can be passed on to customers. Those details are what the market will look for once the full release is reviewed.

The move also fits a broader pattern this week. Investors have been asking whether heavy technology spending is paying off, and the Nasdaq 100 slipped into correction on Monday (Saxo Bank). A company that beats on demand but warns on costs can still lose ground when the sector is nervous.

## What to watch today

Three items matter for the open. First, the Apple reaction itself: whether the 2.8% after-hours decline holds once regular trading begins. Second, the AMD report after the close, which will test whether AI demand is still supporting chip stocks. Third, the election result, which may dominate the tape regardless of company news (Bloomberg). Readers should treat any Apple figures beyond the after-hours move as unconfirmed until the company's own release or a second wire report is reviewed.

## Scope of this update

This article is a pre-market preview and reaction note. It does not restate Apple's revenue, earnings per share or guidance, because those figures were not confirmed in the sources reviewed for this edition.

## Why it matters

Apple's after-hours move points to cost pressure. Memory costs have become a cross-sector issue, which matters for hardware makers and chip suppliers. AMD's report tonight is the next test of AI-driven chip demand, and the market is already sensitive after the Nasdaq 100's slide into correction.

marketImpact.summary: Apple's after-hours drop reflects margin concern, not a demand miss, while AMD's after-close report is a direct test of AI chip sentiment. Both could move semiconductor and hardware names at the open.

tickers.rationale: Slipped 2.8% after hours as memory costs threatened margins (Saxo Bank).
Reports after the close Tuesday; investors will watch AI demand (Yahoo Finance).
